newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian coal miners strike but impact disputed.
newsitem.headline: Russian coal miners strike but impact disputed.

text.p: Angry Russian coal miners pressed on with their nationwide strike on Wednesday, demanding their wages and the government's dismissal.
Industry and union officials gave very different views of the strength of the second day's action as well as contradictory figures for the number still on strike.
A spokeswoman for former state company Rosugol, which runs most coal mines, said 61,000 workers had not turned up for work.
Union leaders put the number of strikers at 400,000.

The issue of wage arrears, affecting almost every sector of the economy, is one of the biggest social and economic problems in Russia. Companies say they cannot pay wages because they are owed money by their own consumers, including the governement.

"According to our data 61,000 miners at 103 of our 175 pits and 21 of 67 open-cast mines were striking today and overnight. Overall there are 445,000 workers in the company," the Rosugol spokeswoman said.
"I cannot imagine how trade unions could say that as many as 400,000 miners were on strike."
Vitaly Budko, head of Coal Miners' Trade Union, told Reuters that the second day of the strike started with about 400,000 miners, or about 80 percent of Russian miners, on strike.
He said 169 pits out of 189 were not working on Wednesday, slightly more than yesterday.
"No one has quit the strike since yesterday," he said.

"I am afraid the strike will grow bigger as many others want to join the protests against wage delays. This may cause a crisis, but unpaid wages for half a year mean the economy has collapsed already."

Union officials said the strike was one of the biggest so far. In the Siberian Kuzbass regions teachers closed a number of schools on Monday and electricity workers in the region, home to more than two million people, planned a protest on Thursday.

But Itar-Tass news agency, quoting local union officials, said the coal strike was already running out of steam in the Kuzbass region, where only 32 pits were involved in industrial action, down from 58 pits yesterday.

The miners have called on Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to quit, blaming his government for the wage delays. A top parliamentary official said on Tuesday that Chernomyrdin could fly to Kuzbass soon to tackle the crisis.
Trade unions officials said the strike would go on until the government met the miners' economic demands.
"Our demands remain the same as the government has made no contacts with us so far," Budko said.

He said the government had paid 471 billion roubles ($85 million) to utilities and residential services in the main mining regions on Monday, but the sum was tiny and the money had never reached the miners themselves.
Union leaders say the government owes the miners at least 1.5 trillion roubles. Consumers owe miners another eight trillion roubles.
Coal mines of the Krasnoyarsk region and in Khakassia in Siberia have decided not to take part in the strike. ($1=5522 Rouble)
